investor_summary:
## Key Drivers

• **Indian banks (ICICI Bank, State Bank of India)** — The RBI aggressively drained liquidity through roughly ₹1 trillion in bond sales and rejected short bond bids, pushing yields higher and raising funding costs across the banking system. With ICICI Bank and SBI among the fund's largest holdings (about 9.2% and 4.2% respectively), this macro tightening was the dominant drag on the fund, compounded by operational disruption flagged at SBI from a nationwide UFBU bank strike.

• **Maruti Suzuki India** — India's largest carmaker fell to a 52-week low as production lagged demand, leaving vehicle shortages ahead of the key festive season. This operational shortfall weighed on the fund through a roughly 2.7% portfolio position.

• **HDFC Bank** — The stock rose about 5% on a CEO succession announcement, bullish brokerage views, and Jefferies' call that foreign investors may reallocate toward Indian financials. As the fund's largest single holding at about 5.7%, this rally provided the most meaningful offset to the week's broad banking weakness. Axis Bank also edged higher on the same foreign-flow theme plus a fresh CLSA bullish call, though the gain was modest.

• **HCL Technologies** — Indian IT stocks rallied sharply on September 15 amid buzz over an AI-related slowdown, with HCL Tech named among the top gainers for a nearly 4% single-day jump. This helped offset some weakness in the fund's other holdings.

## Overall Summary

The fund fell about 1.3% for the week, driven mainly by the RBI's aggressive liquidity drain of roughly ₹1 trillion, which lifted bond yields and funding costs and pressured large banking holdings ICICI Bank and SBI. Maruti Suzuki added to the drag on festive-season vehicle shortages that pushed the stock to a 52-week low. These declines were partially offset by HDFC Bank's roughly 5% gain on its CEO succession and positive brokerage views on foreign flows into Indian financials, alongside an IT sector rally that lifted HCL Technologies. The takeaway: monetary tightening and sector-specific pressures on autos outweighed a strong rebound in select financial and technology names.
